$comment: ARM what-if NOISE allowlist — consumed by scripts/ci/whatif-drift-verdict.mjs.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Microsoft documents the false-positive class directly:
'Some of the properties that are listed as deleted won't actually change.
Properties can be incorrectly reported as deleted when they aren't in the
Bicep file, but are automatically set during deployment as default values.
This result is considered "noise" in the what-if response.'
— https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-resource-manager/bicep/deploy-what-if
RULES OF THE ALLOWLIST (enforced by the script, not by convention):
1. Only propertyChangeType Delete / NoEffect is ever suppressible. A
Create or Modify on a property is a genuine template-vs-live conflict
and is NEVER suppressed.
2. A resource drops out of the drift verdict only when EVERY one of its
property deltas is allowlisted. One unmatched delta keeps the whole
resource as real drift.
3. Every suppressed delta is still printed (step summary + artifact
suppressed-list.txt) so suppression is auditable, never silent.
4. Adding an entry requires a `reason` grounded in the resource's ARM
schema (read-only / server-defaulted / service-managed). Do not add a
property you merely find inconvenient — encode it in bicep instead.
5. A `path` may carry `*` in place of an ARM array index. `*` matches ONLY
digits, in either shape what-if emits (`.0` or `[0]`) — never a property
name — so it cannot blanket a subtree. Add the element form only when a
real what-if run has actually emitted it.
Seeded 2026-07-28 from run 30259654971 (issue #2540): 11/11 Modify deltas
were this class — 9 identical UAMI deltas plus Grafana + the UDF Container
App. See docs/fiab/runbooks/bicep-drift.md.
Extended 2026-09-07 from run 33406666389 (issue #3191). That run's 128 real
resources carried 357 unmatched property deltas; a per-property census of the
raw what-if document (not the 6-per-resource truncated list) showed the
largest families were all server-defaulted or read-only, each confirmed
against its recorded `before` value. The entries added below cover 138 of
those 357 deltas. The rest — AAS asAdministrators, APIM policy bodies,
diagnosticSettings whole log categories, ACR networkRuleSet, KV createMode,
the managedEnvironments block — are REAL template-vs-live conflicts and are
deliberately left in the verdict for a reconciling bicep change.

Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedId.reason: identity.bicep declares no `properties` block (a UAMI has none to set). The RP populates isolationScope='None' (the default of the None|Regional enum, 2024-11-30 schema) plus the read-only clientId/principalId/tenantId. what-if therefore reports the whole `properties` object as Delete on EVERY UAMI in the estate. The subset guard means a future settable property (e.g. assignmentRestrictions) would NOT be suppressed.
Same as above when what-if reports the leaf rather than the parent object. 'None' is the server default; a redeploy that omits it is a no-op.

Microsoft.Dashboard/grafana.reason: Service-managed lifecycle. Azure Managed Grafana upgrades the major version in place; admin-plane/main.bicep deliberately does not pin it (pinning would make a from-scratch deploy fail in any cloud/region where that major is not yet offered — Gov lags Commercial). The template expressing no opinion is the intent, not drift. If Loom ever needs a pinned version, set it in bicep and DELETE this entry.
Read-only — the RP-assigned Grafana URL (surfaced as the grafanaEndpoint output).
Read-only — the exact running Grafana build, chosen by the service.

Microsoft.App/containerApps.reason: Read-only runtime state ('Running'), never settable in a template.
Server-defaulted to 'Consumption' on a Consumption-only managed environment; udf-runtime.bicep omits it deliberately so the same template works on Consumption and workload-profile environments.
Server-defaulted (100). Omitted by template; a redeploy re-applies the same default.
Server-defaulted to [{latestRevision:true, weight:100}] under activeRevisionsMode 'Single'. Declaring it would fight the roll workflows that shift traffic.

Microsoft.Network/privateDnsZones/virtua.reason: Server-defaulted. `resolutionPolicy` was added in the 2024-06-01 privateDnsZones schema as a Default|NxDomainRedirect enum; the RP stamps 'Default' on every link, including the ~27 links private-dns.bicep creates without expressing an opinion. Measured before='Default' on every occurrence in run 33406666389 — a redeploy that omits it re-applies the same value. If Loom ever needs NxDomainRedirect, set it in bicep and DELETE this entry.

Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints.reason: Server-defaulted to false. A dual-stack flag the RP stamps on every private endpoint under the newer network API versions; private-endpoint.bicep declares only IPv4 subnets, so what-if reports the RP's own false as a deletion. Measured before=false on every occurrence in run 33406666389.

Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints/priva.reason: Read-only — the ARM resource ID the RP assigns to each generated privateDnsZoneConfigs child. The template declares each config by name + privateDnsZoneId only; the full child ID is never settable.
Read-only — RP-assigned concurrency tag on each generated config.
Read-only — the ARM type discriminator ('Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints/privateDnsZoneGroups/privateDnsZoneConfigs') the RP stamps on each generated config.
Read-only lifecycle state ('Succeeded'), never settable in a template.

Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings.reason: Server-defaulted remnant of a RETIRED feature. Diagnostic-setting-level retention was retired in favour of Log Analytics workspace / storage lifecycle retention; the RP still materializes `retentionPolicy:{enabled:false,days:0}` on every category. Measured before=0 on every occurrence in run 33406666389, so a redeploy that omits it re-applies the same zero. NOTE: this suppresses ONLY the retention leaf — a Delete of a whole `properties.logs.N` category (the template declaring fewer categories than live) stays real drift and keeps the resource in the verdict.

Server-defaulted remnant of the same retired retention feature, on the metrics side: the RP materializes `retentionPolicy:{enabled:false,days:0}` on every metric category. Measured before=0 on every occurrence in run 33406666389.

Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/sq.reason: Cosmos DB's documented default indexing policy. A container created without an explicit indexingPolicy is stamped with includedPaths=[{path:'/*'}] — measured verbatim as the before value in run 33406666389. Because only a Delete is ever suppressible (rule 1), this can only fire when the template declares no indexing policy for that container, in which case live IS the server default by construction.
The other half of Cosmos DB's default indexing policy: excludedPaths=[{path:'/"_etag"/?'}], the system-managed _etag exclusion. Measured verbatim as the before value in run 33406666389.

Same default _etag exclusion, for the containers where what-if reported the array ELEMENT rather than the whole array. Both granularities occur in run 33406666389 and which one ARM emits is not stable.

Read-only projection of the ACCOUNT-level backup policy onto the container. backupPolicy is settable on Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts, not on a container; the RP echoes the account's policy ({type:1} = Continuous, measured in run 33406666389) into every container's resource body. cosmos.bicep sets it once on the account, which is the correct place.

Server-defaulted. Under the default LastWriterWins conflict-resolution mode Cosmos stamps conflictResolutionPath='/_ts' — measured verbatim in run 33406666389. The templates declare no conflict-resolution policy, so the RP default is re-applied on redeploy.

Microsoft.ApiManagement/service.reason: Server-defaulted, and defaulted to the SECURE value. APIM stamps the legacy-protocol toggles as 'False' (disabled) when the template does not mention them — measured before='False' in run 33406666389 — so omitting it neither enables SSL 3.0 nor changes anything on redeploy. Suppressing it does NOT drop the APIM service from the verdict: that resource also carries Modify deltas (developerPortalStatus, legacyPortalStatus, natGatewayState) which rule 1 never suppresses.
Same legacy-protocol toggle on the backend (gateway-to-backend) side. Measured before='False' — the secure default — in run 33406666389.
Same legacy-protocol toggle on the backend side. Measured before='False' — the secure default — in run 33406666389.
